0:0.en: My name is Lucía and I live in Seville.

0:1.en: I get up at seven in the morning.

0:2.en: First I shower and then I have breakfast.

0:3.en: I drink a coffee with milk and a toast with oil and tomato.

1:1.en: I go to work by bicycle, because the office is close.

1:2.en: I work at a travel agency with two very nice colleagues.

2:0.en: At noon I eat at a bar in the square.

2:1.en: The waiter already knows what I want: a salad and cold water.

2:2.en: In Seville it is very hot.

0:2.en: I am in Oaxaca, in Mexico, with my sister.

0:3.en: The city is very beautiful and it has houses of many colors.

1:0.en: The hotel is small, but the room is big and clean.

1:1.en: In the morning we eat fruit and sweet bread.

1:2.en: Afterward we walked through the city center and visited the markets.

2:0.en: The food here is delicious, but it's very spicy.

2:1.en: My sister eats everything, but I always order water.

0:0.en: Last Sunday I went to an old café in Buenos Aires with my friend Sofía.

0:1.en: We arrived at five in the afternoon and there were almost no free tables.

0:2.en: In the end we sat down next to the window.

1:0.en: I ordered a coffee with milk and two medialunas.

1:1.en: Sofía ordered a tea and a slice of apple pie.

1:2.en: The waiter was an older man who was wearing a white jacket.

2:0.en: At the next table, two men were playing chess and not talking.

2:1.en: Further away, a girl was writing in a notebook.

2:2.en: We (females) talked for two hours about work, family, and vacations.

3:0.en: When we left, it was already nighttime and it was cold.

3:1.en: I paid, because she paid last time.

0:0.en: Last night I returned home very late.

0:1.en: I went up to the third floor, took out the key, and opened the door.

0:2.en: Everything was dark, but I didn't turn on the light so as not to wake up my roommate.

1:0.en: I went to the kitchen and drank a glass of water.

1:1.en: The refrigerator was in another place and it seemed strange to me.

1:2.en: Afterwards I saw a cat on top of the table.

1:3.en: We do not have a cat.

2:1.en: A lady in pajamas looked at me from the door with a slipper in her hand.

2:2.en: I shouted, she shouted, and the cat jumped to the floor.

3:1.en: My apartment is the fourth one, not the third one.

3:2.en: I apologized to him/her many times.

3:3.en: She laughed and told me: "Calm down, son, my door never closes properly."

1:0.en: I am writing to you to express my dissatisfaction with the stay I spent at your hotel in Valencia from May 12 to 15.

2:0.en: Also, the air conditioning was not working.

1:1.en: I had booked a double room with sea views, but when I arrived they gave me an interior room that faced a courtyard.

2:1.en: I notified reception twice and they promised me that a technician would come up that same afternoon.

3:0.en: I understand that during peak season there may be problems.

2:2.en: However, no one came and we had to sleep three nights with the window open and a lot of noise.

3:1.en: Even so, I believe I paid for a service that I did not receive.

3:2.en: That's why I'm asking you to return me the price difference between the two rooms.

3:3.en: If I do not receive a response within fifteen days, I will file an official complaint.

4:0.en: I would like to return to Valencia next year, and I would stay at your hotel again if this matter were resolved well.

0:0.en: In many countries people think that all Spaniards take a nap every day.

0:1.en: Reality is different: most people work in the afternoon and don't have time.

0:2.en: However, I believe that we should recover this custom.

1:0.en: First of all, the siesta is good for health.

1:1.en: According to several studies, twenty minutes of rest improve memory and mood.

1:2.en: Also, in summer it gets so hot at noon that it is almost impossible to concentrate.

2:0.en: On the other hand, I understand those who do not agree.

2:1.en: If we stop for two hours to eat and rest, we leave work very late and see little of our family.

2:2.en: My brother, who lives in Bilbao, says that he would prefer to finish at five and forget about the nap.

3:0.en: In conclusion, it's not necessary to choose between all or nothing.

3:1.en: If companies offered more flexible schedules, each person could decide.

3:2.en: I, for my part, will keep closing my eyes for a little while after eating.

3:3.en: Tomorrow I'll be in a better mood, for sure.

0:0.en: The Villaseca del Monte Town Council, a village of barely eighty inhabitants in the province of Teruel, has launched a campaign to attract new families.

0:1.en: The offer includes a house with symbolic rent and a job at the only bar in the town, which has been closed since January.

1:1.en: When the bar closes, social life ends.

1:2.en: We are looking for someone who wants to stay, not someone who comes to try their luck for a summer.

1:0.en: We don't want the people to die, explained yesterday the mayor, Pilar Navarro.

2:0.en: The news has spread like wildfire on social media.

1:3.en: The main condition is that the family has at least two school-age children, since the school risks closing if it does not reach five students.

2:1.en: In just one week, the City Council has received more than three thousand applications, many of them from Argentina, Colombia, and Venezuela.

2:3.en: I wish we could take everyone in, said the mayor.

3:0.en: Not all the neighbors look at it favorably.

3:1.en: Some people fear that the newcomers will leave as soon as the first winter arrives.

3:2.en: Even so, most people trust that this time will be different.

3:3.en: The name of the chosen family will be announced at the end of the month, and the bar will reopen, if everything goes well, before the August holidays.

0:0.en: Few words are as difficult to translate as 'sobremesa'.

0:2.en: That our language has needed a term to name it says a lot about those of us who speak it.

0:1.en: It doesn't refer to a dessert or a piece of furniture, but rather that imprecise time that passes after eating, when the plates are empty and no one has the slightest intention of getting up.

1:0.en: At my grandparents' house, in a village in Castile, Sunday after-lunch conversation lasted until the light began to fade.

1:2.en: As a child, I thought it was a tedious procedure.

1:1.en: There, politics were discussed without anyone convincing anyone, old anecdotes were retold, and small family conflicts were either resolved or worsened.

1:3.en: Today I suspect that in those apparently sterile hours what kept us united was being woven.

2:0.en: It will be objected to me that such a custom is a luxury incompatible with the current pace, and it will not lack reason for whoever says so.

2:2.en: However, it is advisable to ask ourselves what we lose when we measure time solely by its productivity.

3:0.en: Both in Madrid and in Lima or Montevideo, I have verified that after-dinner conversation survives wherever someone dares not to look at the clock.

2:1.en: We eat quickly, often alone and in front of a screen, and we have replaced conversation with an incessant exchange of short messages.

3:1.en: It does not require tablecloths made of thread or large banquets.

3:2.en: All it takes is a cooling cup of coffee, some crumbs on the table, and the willingness to listen.

3:3.en: Perhaps defending her is, in its own way, a discreet form of resistance.
